# jwt_auth

Verifies a JSON Web Token and optionally maps it to a consumer.

| | |
|---|---|
| Runs | before the request is forwarded |
| Default priority | 2400 (higher runs earlier) |
| Attach to | a route, a service, a workspace, or every request (`global`, system workspace only) |
| Switch off everywhere | flag `plugin_jwt_auth` set to `false` |

## Configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer` (required) | string |  | The iss claim must equal this. |
| `audiences` | list of string | `[]` | When not empty, the aud claim must contain one of these. |
| `jwks_url` | string |  | Where the signing keys are published. |
| `jwks` | object |  | Signing keys inline, as a JSON Web Key Set. |
| `jwks.keys` (required) | list of object |  |  |
| `secret` | secret |  | Shared secret for HS256. |
| `algorithms` | list of `RS256`, `RS384`, `RS512`, `ES256`, `ES384`, `EdDSA`, `HS256` | `["RS256","ES256"]` |  |
| `leeway_secs` | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 600) | `60` | Clock difference tolerated for exp and nbf. |
| `token_sources` | list of string | `["header:Authorization"]` |  |
| `required` | boolean | `true` | When false, a request with no token passes unauthenticated. |
| `consumer_claim` | string |  | A claim whose value must equal a consumer custom_id. |
| `claims_to_headers` | object | `{}` | Claim name to the request header that carries it upstream. |
| `jwks_cache_secs` | integer (≥ 10, ≤ 86400) | `300` |  |
| `anonymous` | string |  | A consumer name to run as when no token is presented. |

## When to use it

When callers already hold a signed token from an identity provider. The gateway checks the signature, the issuer, the expiry and (when you list any) the audience, so your upstream does not have to. A token can also be mapped to a consumer, so limits and access rules written for consumers apply.

## Examples

Verify tokens against the provider's published keys, and pass two claims to the upstream as headers:

```yaml
version: 1
services:
  - name: accounts
    backends:
      - target: "10.0.0.7:8080"
routes:
  - name: accounts-api
    service: accounts
    paths: [/accounts]
    plugins:
      - type: jwt_auth
        config:
          issuer: https://login.example.com/
          jwks_url: https://login.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
          audiences: [accounts-api]
          claims_to_headers:
            sub: X-User-Id
            tenant: X-Tenant
```

Tokens signed with a shared secret, each mapped to a consumer by its `sub` claim:

```yaml
version: 1
services:
  - name: partners
    backends:
      - target: "10.0.0.8:8080"
routes:
  - name: partner-api
    service: partners
    paths: [/partner]
    plugins:
      - type: jwt_auth
        config:
          issuer: partner-portal
          algorithms: [HS256]
          secret: { $env: APG_SECRET_PARTNER_JWT }
          consumer_claim: sub
          leeway_secs: 10
consumers:
  - name: acme
    custom_id: acme-corp
```

## What clients and upstreams see

- A missing, expired, wrongly signed or wrongly addressed token: `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`. The message does not say which check failed.
- The key set cannot be fetched and no copy is held yet: `503 AUTH_UNAVAILABLE`. Once fetched, the copy keeps being used while the provider is unreachable.
- Tokens with `alg: none`, or an algorithm you did not list, are refused.

## Goes well with

`acl` once tokens are mapped to consumers; `rate_limit` with `scope: consumer`. Keys published at `jwks_url` are fetched again after `jwks_cache_secs`, and at once (at most every 30 seconds) when a token names a key the copy does not hold.
